title: Security scan
description: What a closed taxonomy of security patterns matched in a named set of source files. The taxonomy is an enum rather than prose so that two scans of one file set are comparable and a thirteenth pattern cannot be invented at scan time. `scanned` and `patterns_not_evaluated` are required beside `findings` because an empty findings array means nothing without them: a clean scan over two of the eight changed files, or a scan whose dependency check had no audit result to read, would otherwise be indistinguishable from a clean scan of everything. No field carries an action or a verdict — foundation/0005 R5 keeps a specialized agent from choosing what runs next, and the agent this taxonomy comes from decided block_tc, which is exactly that.

contract_version.description: A consumer rejects an artifact it was not built to read rather than inferring version from shape.

scan_id.description: Stable identifier for this scan, supplied by the caller and never minted by the producer: a scan stamped from a clock could not be repeated and compared.

producer.description: What performed the scan. Not a const: the contract requires the artifact, not a particular producer of it.

scanned.description: Every path the scan covered, repository-root-relative. Required so a clean result states what it was clean over.

patterns_not_evaluated.description: Patterns that could not be applied because an input they depend on was absent — a dependency audit result, or a declared security profile. Empty means all twelve were applied. An unevaluated pattern reported as clean is the failure this field exists to prevent.

findings.description: One entry per match, sorted by file then line. Empty is a real result and the common one.

severity.description: What the match gives an attacker. About the match, never about the file it sits in or the cost of the fix: a critical finding in unreachable code is still critical, and reachability belongs in the reason.

cwe.description: The Common Weakness Enumeration identifier for the matched pattern, so a finding resolves against a taxonomy this contract does not own.

symbol.description: The enclosing function, method, or handler where one exists. Absent at file scope.

evidence.description: The construct that triggered the match, copied exactly rather than paraphrased. Where the match is an absence, the enclosing construct that lacks the check. A finding whose evidence cannot be quoted is a finding that was not observed.

reason.description: What an attacker gets, in terms of this code. Not a restatement of the pattern name, which the type field already carries.

notes.description: Anything a reader needs to interpret the result that no other field holds: an absent security profile, a construct that worried the producer and matched no pattern. Never a finding — the taxonomy is closed and findings is where matches go.

pattern.description: The closed taxonomy. Adding a pattern is a contract version change, so that a consumer can tell a scan that could not have matched a pattern from one that did not.
